How long have you been here?
I have already booked the next one.

I have been doing this for eleven years now, and people always ask me the same thing. What is the best place you have ever been to? I never have a good answer. I have driven through forty-one states. I have slept in parking lots, in national parks, and once, by accident, in a cemetery. But I have never taken a trip that went the way I planned it. That is the honest answer. Every good thing that has happened to me out here happened because something went wrong first. I have missed two connections in my life, and both times I met somebody at the gate who changed where I was going. So no, I do not have a favorite place. I have a favorite kind of day, and it is the day the plan falls apart before lunch.

I am fifty-two years old, and until March I had never left the country. Never. My passport arrived in the mail and I just looked at it on the kitchen table for a week. Then my daughter booked the whole trip for me. Sixteen hours, one layover in Amsterdam, and an itinerary she printed out and put in my jacket pocket, because she knows me. And here is the part nobody warned me about. I was not scared on the plane. I was scared in the line, when the officer asked me a question and I had to answer in a language I have studied since school and never once spoken out loud. Four words. That was the whole test. I have been back three weeks now, I am still jet-lagged, and I have already asked her to book the next one.
